heading.purpose: Modal titles, page titles, section headers — plain system sans, 600 weight, 18-20px. Confirmed directly against src/index.css h1/h2/h3 rule. Not mono/uppercase; the navbar wordmark's mono/amber treatment is a standalone brand mark, not the heading default.

body.purpose: Default paragraph and control text; the root 15px font.

label.purpose: Difficulty placards, tab labels, captions — 11px uppercase.

mono.purpose: Code, console, IDs, level-card names, key legends, navbar wordmark. Never decorative on prose/headings. Carries a Thai fallback ('Leelawadee UI', 'Noto Sans Thai') because some mono-styled content carries translated Thai text.

segment.purpose: CSS-built 7-segment digits (no font) for every timed/counted value — elapsed, off-track, best time, Result Modal time, leaderboard star/levels-passed tallies.

shadows.name: recessed-glass
shadows.purpose: SevenSegmentDisplay's housing only — a display window set into the bezel. Confirmed as the only box-shadow declaration in the shipped src/ stylesheets; nothing else uses one.

motionMeta.numericValues: Instant segment swap — never eased or tweened (the Instant-Segment Rule); applies only to SevenSegmentDisplay content, not chrome.
motionMeta.reducedMotion: Global @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) override in src/index.css collapses all chrome animation/transition durations to ~0.

components.name: Seven-Segment Display
components.description: The system's signature component — real LED segment digits built from CSS clip-path shapes (no webfont), recessed behind an inset-shadow housing. Ghost (unlit) cells always visible. Value changes are instant, never tweened.
components.html: 05.3
components.css: .ds-segment-display { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 3px 4px; background: #0a0908; border-radius: 2px; box-shadow: inset 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.6); font-family: ui-monospace, Consolas, monospace; } .ds-digit { display: inline-block; width: 12px; height: 20px; margin: 0 1px; text-align: center; line-height: 20px; color: #3a2f1a; } .ds-digit--on { color: #ff9d00; text-shadow: 0 0 4px rgba(255,157,0,0.5); }

components.name: Run Key (Primary Button)
components.description: Solid amber fill — the one key the whole console is built around. Same treatment reused for login/onboarding submits and the Result Modal's Try Again (which additionally pops in on mount, since it resolves an attempt).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #ffb020; color: #1a1204; font: 700 12px/1.2 system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.04em; padding: 10px 20px; border: 1px solid #ffc966; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms ease-out, transform 120ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #ffc966; transform: scale(1.03); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.96); transition-duration: 60ms; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ffb020; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Secondary Key
components.description: Bordered ghost key — Pause/Step/Reset, nav actions, admin actions. Uppercase mono-weight label; border-only hover keeps it distinct from the amber primary.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: #17150f; color: #f5f2e8; font: 600 12px/1.2 system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.04em; padding: 6px 14px; border: 1px solid #322e26; border-radius: 3px; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 150ms ease-out, transform 100ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover:not(:disabled) { border-color: #ffb020; } .ds-btn-secondary:active:not(:disabled) { transform: scale(0.94); transition-duration: 60ms; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ffb020; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-secondary:disabled { opacity: 0.4; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Level Card (Heat Placard)
components.description: Selectable level entry styled as a competition heat placard: a bordered difficulty tag (not plain text), star-pips, and a small segment-display best time. Incomplete levels show plain text, never a fake 00.0 reading.
components.css: .ds-card-level { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; width: 100%; padding: 10px 12px; border: 1px solid #322e26; border-radius: 4px; background: #17150f; text-align: left; cursor: pointer; font-family: system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; transition: border-color 150ms ease-out, background-color 150ms ease-out, transform 120ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-card-level:hover { border-color: #ffb020; } .ds-card-level:active { transform: scale(0.98); } .ds-card-level--selected { border-color: #ffb020; background: rgba(255,176,32,0.12); } .ds-card-level__header { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: baseline; gap: 8px; } .ds-card-level__name { font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; font-family: ui-monospace, Consolas, monospace; color: #f5f2e8; } .ds-card-level__difficulty { padding: 1px 6px; border: 1px solid #322e26; border-radius: 2px; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.04em; color: #8a8577; } .ds-card-level__best { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; } .ds-pips { display: inline-flex; gap: 3px; } .ds-pip { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background: rgba(216,212,201,0.07); } .ds-pip--lit { background: #34d058; }

components.name: Underline Tab
components.description: Left-panel and admin-dashboard tab — bottom-border indicator in Signal Amber when active, no fill/pill treatment.
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: flex; border-bottom: 1px solid #322e26; font-family: system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-tab { flex: 1; padding: 10px 8px; border: none; background: none; color: #8a8577; font-size: 13px; cursor: pointer; border-bottom: 2px solid transparent; transition: color 150ms ease-out, border-color 150ms ease-out; } .ds-tab:hover { color: #f5f2e8; } .ds-tab--active { color: #f5f2e8; border-bottom-color: #ffb020; }

components.name: Result Modal (Scoreboard Flash)
components.description: Signature pass/fail overlay — plain sans heading (not mono/uppercase — see the Hierarchy note on the reverted placard treatment), flat-filled star-pips + green segment-display time (or muted fail reason), Try Again as the resolving pop-in beat.

components.css: .ds-result-overlay { position: absolute; inset: 0; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.7); } .ds-result-modal { min-width: 260px; padding: 24px; border-radius: 3px; background: #17150f; border: 1px solid #322e26; text-align: center; font-family: system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-result-title { margin: 0 0 12px; font-size: 18px; font-weight: 600; } .ds-result-title--passed { color: #34d058; } .ds-result-time { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 6px; margin: 12px 0 18px; } .ds-result-time__label { font-size: 11px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.06em; color: #8a8577; } .ds-pips { display: inline-flex; gap: 10px; } .ds-pip { width: 14px; height: 14px; border-radius: 50%; background: rgba(216,212,201,0.07); } .ds-pip--lit { background: #34d058; } .ds-btn-primary { margin-top: 18px; border-radius: 4px; }

narrative.overview:
This is a redesign - the app's second visual identity, replacing 'The Circuit Board' (a flat, purple-accented, bordered system) wholesale rather than extending it. It was chosen through a structured direction roll (concept-seed.mjs --scope direction --mode operate, seed 444573ff): the assigned grounded candidate was a literal circuit-board/silkscreen reading, but a dealt challenger - the seven-segment display family (bedside clocks, gas-station price totems, scoreboards) - won on both audience identification and product clarity and became the build.

Every number in this app is a real LED segment digit, not a themed numeral font, because the product's core feedback loop - elapsed time, off-track time, best times, star counts - genuinely is a timing instrument's job. The interface is a matte, near-black instrument bezel: silkscreen off-white labels, one amber signal for anything live or interactive, red and green reserved strictly for running/pass outcomes, exactly like a real scoreboard's lamp colors. This is a classroom tool for Thai mid/high-school robotics students, run by a teacher, so legibility and instant state-reading still come first.

The simulation canvas stays its own fixed, mode-independent palette, unrelated to the app chrome's tokens - that boundary survived the redesign unchanged.
keyCharacteristics: Every timed/counted value renders as real 7-segment digits (SevenSegmentDisplay, CSS-built, no webfont) - ghost cells always visible, value changes are instant, never a tween.
Matte near-black bezel, always dark - no light mode, a deliberate identity commitment.
One accent: amber, for anything live/interactive/primary - including the single Run key.
Red and green are reserved for outcome states (running/live, pass) - never decoration.
Sharp, small corner radii (2-5px) - a milled panel edge, not a soft rounded card.
Flat by default, with one motivated exception: segment-display glass is recessed behind an inset shadow.
Thai gets its own system-font stack, line-height, and :lang(th) sync - unchanged from before the redesign.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Amber marks exactly one focal thing per view - the active tab, the selected card, the primary/Run action. It never doubles as decoration.

rules.name: The Segment-First Rule
rules.body: Any value that is a duration, a time, or a count renders through SevenSegmentDisplay, not plain text - that's what makes this a scoreboard and not a dashboard with numbers on it.

rules.name: The No-Light-Mode Rule
rules.body: This world commits to dark only. Do not add a prefers-color-scheme: light branch back - a scoreboard's bezel doesn't change color with the room.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces sit flush with their background at rest - shadows are reserved for the one recessed-glass exception, nowhere else.

rules.name: The Instant-Segment Rule
rules.body: Numeric readouts never animate their own value change - no easing, no count-up. Everything else may still use the shared motion vocabulary.

rules.name: The One Motion Vocabulary Rule
rules.body: Tactile chrome (buttons, cards, modal, tabs) reuses one set of values: scale, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), 60-350ms, --accent-hover for the pressed state.

rules.name: The Lang-Follows-Language Rule
rules.body: document.documentElement.lang stays in sync with useLanguageStore at all times - unchanged by the redesign, independent of visual world.

dos: Do render every timed/counted value through SevenSegmentDisplay - never plain text for a number the product is timing.
Do keep numeric value changes instant, no easing; reserve the shared eased motion vocabulary for chrome.
Do keep Signal Amber to one focal element per screen.
Do use --on-accent for any text placed on an amber fill - never white.
Do scale radius with a surface's size on the confirmed 2/3/4/5px steps.
Do reuse the level card's selected pattern (accent border + --accent-bg wash) as the one selection idiom.
Do keep the simulation canvas's palette self-contained and independent of the app chrome's tokens.
Do keep document.documentElement.lang in sync with useLanguageStore.
donts: Don't add a prefers-color-scheme: light branch back - this world is dark-only by identity.
Don't add box-shadow anywhere except the segment-display recessed-glass exception.
Don't introduce a second accent hue; amber is the only interactive signal.
Don't put white text on an amber fill - use --on-accent.
Don't load a custom webfont, including for the segment digits - they're CSS shapes, no network request needed.
Don't use monospace decoratively on prose or headings.
Don't let the simulation canvas's colors bleed into app-chrome UI, or vice versa.
Don't animate a SevenSegmentDisplay value with a tween/count-up - it must jump.
Don't animate on every re-render or add page-load choreography that delays interaction.
